qas.q: What is the minimum order quantity, and where does Linker deliver?
qas.a: There is no pallet minimum. Orders start from individual units, delivered across the EU. Equipment ships according to project schedules, with trade quotes detailing destination freight.

qas.q: Can different brands be combined in one project order?
qas.a: Yes. Inverters, batteries, smart meters, and accessories from different brands can be combined in one order. They ship together under a unified invoice; check each pairing against the compatibility lists on file before ordering.

qas.q: Does Linker supply complete storage packages or individual components?
qas.a: Both. Installers can order packaged systems with matching balance-of-system components, or source individual replacement units and accessories.

qas.q: How are project quotations processed?
qas.a: Quotations include confirmed B2B net pricing, a full bill of materials, and applicable freight terms for the project destination.

qas.q: How do trade partners access net pricing?
qas.a: Wholesale net pricing is visible to verified partner accounts. Unregistered contractors can submit project parameters to receive a formal trade quotation.

qas.q: Who is eligible for a Partner Account?
qas.a: Professional solar installers, electrical contractors (Elektrofachbetriebe), and EPCs operating within the EU. Registrations are reviewed individually before account activation.

qas.q: How are lithium battery systems transported?
qas.a: Batteries are classified as dangerous goods (Class 9) and transported via certified freight carriers. Systems carry UN38.3 transport certification, with compliant crating and documentation managed by Linker.

qas.q: What is the procedure if transport damage occurs?
qas.a: Note visible packaging or pallet damage on the freight receipt (CMR) at delivery. Linker coordinates carrier claims and replacement units to avoid project downtime.

qas.q: What delivery destinations are supported?
qas.a: Deliveries route directly to your company warehouse, branch location, or scheduled project sites across the European Union.

qas.q: Whose warranty applies to the supplied equipment?
qas.a: Statutory B2B warranty rights apply, and product guarantees apply as issued in the documents on the product pages and in this library. Linker handles any claim for you, from your order.

qas.q: How are warranty claims processed?
qas.a: Open Warranty & Replacements from your order. The signed-in account confirms the order, and the form keeps the serial number, model, and fault description with that order. Linker handles the diagnostic exchange with the manufacturer's technical desk. Open Warranty & Replacements .

qas.q: What technical support is included with an order?
qas.a: Linker provides sizing tools and wiring references before the order, and live commissioning troubleshooting from the engineering desk in Germany.

qas.q: Is equipment certified for the German electrical grid?
qas.a: Grid compliance is documented per model: inverters for low-voltage connection need a Unit Certificate (Einheitenzertifikat) and NA-Schutz documentation under VDE-AR-N 4105, medium-voltage systems follow VDE-AR-N 4110. Linker requests the certificates for the models in your order.

qas.q: Are documentation and manuals available in German?
qas.a: Datasheets and manuals are on file in English, and in German where a German edition exists. Linker's engineering desk helps with technical questions on any of them.

qas.q: Are Declarations of Conformity provided with orders?
qas.a: Yes, on request: Linker requests the CE Declarations of Conformity and relevant test certificates for the models in your order.

qas.q: What technical documentation is available through Genie?
qas.a: Genie indexes the datasheets, manuals, and compatibility matrices in this library, retrieving specific technical parameters and wiring requirements directly.

qas.q: What is the maximum wire gauge accepted by the DTSU666 direct terminals?
qas.a: Up to 16 mm². The current terminals of the DTSU666 accept conductors with a cross-sectional area of up to 16 mm²; the RS485 terminals take 0.25 to 1 mm².

qas.q: Can one bridge join different battery models?
qas.a: No. The bridge guide requires the two units joined by one bracket to have the same model specification. It names EF BD-5.1-S1, EF BD-5-S2 and EF BD-8-S2 as applicable battery types.

qas.q: How many bridge kits should I order for two towers?
qas.a: One ordered kit is the full pack shown in the manual: two bridge brackets, four M5 × 12 screws and four M5 studs. The guide recommends securing both sides of each module; its example of two six-module towers needs 12 brackets, or six of these kits.

qas.q: What gap must I leave between the two tower bases?
qas.a: With PowerOcean bases, the bridge guide specifies 95.4–105.4 mm between bases; with OCEAN 2 bases, it specifies 94.6–104.5 mm. These are base-to-base gaps for the bridged layout.

qas.q: How many EF BD-5-S2 modules fit one floor or wall tower?
qas.a: The 5 kWh battery manual permits up to six modules per floor-standing tower and up to three per wall-mounted tower. The inverter’s own module limit also applies to a multi-tower order.

qas.q: Can an existing EF BD-5.1-S1 tower be extended with EF BD-5-S2?
qas.a: For the P1-S2 mixed-stack installation, the guide names exactly these two modules. It recommends the earlier EF BD-B-S1 base, with EF BD-5.1-S1 modules below and EF BD-5-S2 modules above. That installation order applies; an older stack does not necessarily have the same parts.

qas.q: What should I record when planning an older tower extension?
qas.a: Use “Extend an existing system” from this product page and record the existing module model, base model, current count and intended new count. For the documented P1-S2 mixed stack, those identities are EF BD-5.1-S1, EF BD-B-S1 and this EF BD-5-S2. A Project sent to Linker is tied to its saved version, so the arrangement you describe stays identifiable. Our engineers recommend the arrangement from the installation guide before the order.

qas.q: What warranty applies to the EF BD-5-S2?
qas.a: 15 years retaining 60% of usable energy, or 21.9 MWh throughput, whichever comes first. The period starts on the earlier of commissioning (activation) and nine months after the production date, and it transfers with proof of ownership transfer. Coverage is Europe excluding Sweden.

qas.q: Can the OCEAN 2 5 kWh and EF BD-8-S2 modules share a tower?
qas.a: The 8 kWh battery manual explicitly describes mixed stacking with the OCEAN 2 5 kWh battery. The complete installation drawing sets the module sequence, the tower height and the inverter limit before the order.

qas.q: Is a battery base shown in the EF BD-8-S2 module box?
qas.a: No base is listed in the manual’s 8 kWh battery-module box: it shows the B1 module and its mounting pieces, bolts and screws. The same manual depicts the battery base as a separate system component, so include the required base in the tower parts list.

qas.q: What site clearance matters for the 8 kWh module’s cooling?
qas.a: The illustrated single-tower layout needs at least 300 mm above and on both sides, with 65–85 mm to the rear wall. Side-by-side towers need at least 300 mm between them. The air exhausts need clear space; blocked airflow can cause overheating and power derating.

qas.q: What warranty applies to the EF BD-8-S2?
qas.a: 10 years retaining 70% of usable energy, or 29.97 MWh throughput, whichever comes first. An optional five-year extension to 15 years at 60% / 35.1 MWh is available through an authorized installer within 12 months of the warranty start date. The period starts on the earlier of commissioning (activation) and nine months after the production date, and it transfers with proof of ownership transfer. Coverage is Europe excluding Sweden.

qas.q: How many MPPTs does GW10K-EHA-G20 have?
qas.a: 4 MPPTs, strings 1/1/1/1, 20 A maximum MPPT current and 26 A short-circuit current. Maximum PV input power is 20.0 kW. The MPPT window is 40–560 V; at nominal power it is 190~500 V.

qas.q: Which battery modules stack with this power module?

qas.q: How many BAT-D modules can one GW10K-ETA-G20 column take?

qas.q: What backup load can the GW10K-ETA-G20 design support?

After a grid outage, connected loads above 1.1 times rated inverter power cause overload shutdown. Protected circuits are sized to the continuous limit, not the 10-second peak.

qas.q: Which meter and CT arrangement must be planned for this inverter?

The quote lists an external meter and any additional CTs as line items before installation.
qas.product: GoodWe ESA GW10K-ETA-G20 (10 kW three-phase power module)

qas.q: What does one GW125/261-ESA-LCN-G10 cabinet contain?
qas.a: One cabinet holds the 125 kW power conversion system (PCS), five battery packs of 52.25 kWh each (261.25 kWh), the local control module for energy management, the liquid-cooling unit, a dehumidifier, the aerosol fire-extinguishing device with smoke and temperature detectors, and the AC and DC circuit breakers. Delivered with it are four expansion bolts, the Wi-Fi antenna, five MSD switches, cable terminals and the documentation. The AC cable, the protective earth conductor, the upstream circuit breaker, the meter with current transformers and a SEC3000C controller are not part of the cabinet.
qas.product: GoodWe ESA GW125/261-ESA-LCN-G10 (125 kW / 261 kWh all-in-one storage cabinet)

qas.q: How is the cabinet connected to the grid?
qas.a: The cabinet is connected on the AC side to a 400 V three-phase supply (3L / N / PE). TN-S, TN-C, TN-C-S and TT systems are supported; an IT system needs an external isolation transformer. Plan a dedicated upstream circuit breaker for each cabinet (recommended rating 250 A) with no other loads on it. In TT systems a residual-current device is required; 100 mA at the upstream breaker is recommended. The cables enter the cabinet from below.
qas.product: GoodWe ESA GW125/261-ESA-LCN-G10 (125 kW / 261 kWh all-in-one storage cabinet)

qas.q: Which VDE grid-connection certificates are available?
qas.a: Two documents are available as downloads on this page: the certificate of conformity for VDE-AR-N 4105:2018-11 (TÜV Rheinland, issued 20 May 2025) and the unit certificate for VDE-AR-N 4110, 4120 and 4130 (SGS, No. 250008RECO10-CER, valid until 12 December 2030). The VDE-AR-N 4105 certificate notes that above 30 kVA the integrated interface switch has to work together with a central grid and plant protection (NA-Schutz). The unit certificate notes that the cabinet has no test terminal block; one is fitted separately where required.
qas.product: GoodWe ESA GW125/261-ESA-LCN-G10 (125 kW / 261 kWh all-in-one storage cabinet)

qas.q: What is needed for power limiting at the grid connection point and for several cabinets?
qas.a: For power limiting at the grid connection point, a meter with current transformers is installed there: a GM330 smart meter with CTs of ratio nA/5A, or, where the site cannot be switched off, a DTSD1352 secondary meter with secondary CTs fitted on the existing primary CTs. Several cabinets are run by a SEC3000C controller over LAN: up to 20 cabinets in a daisy-chain connection and up to 15 in a star connection, together with grid-tied PV inverters. A third-party energy management system is connected over LAN or RS485; it then sets the number of cabinets. The cabinet's communication protocols are Modbus TCP and Modbus RTU. Cabinets in one system should be the same model.
qas.product: GoodWe ESA GW125/261-ESA-LCN-G10 (125 kW / 261 kWh all-in-one storage cabinet)

qas.q: Can the cabinet supply the site when the grid fails?
qas.a: Not on its own. Switching between grid-connected and off-grid operation needs a GoodWe STS switching cabinet, which is a separate device and not part of this article. The cabinet may stand at most 45 m from the STS when the two communicate directly, and the state-of-charge range is set to 10% to 90% for this mode. With an uninterruptible power supply between the STS and the SEC3000C, the system can be black-started remotely.
qas.product: GoodWe ESA GW125/261-ESA-LCN-G10 (125 kW / 261 kWh all-in-one storage cabinet)

qas.q: What does the site need for delivery and installation?
qas.a: The cabinet measures 1050 × 2250 × 1400 mm (W × H × D) and weighs 2580 kg. It is moved by crane with lifting slings rated at 5 t or more each, or by a forklift with a load capacity of 5 t or more, and stands on a level, load-bearing foundation of concrete or another non-combustible material with a cable entry from below. It is suitable for indoor and outdoor installation (IP54) at -25 to +55 °C and up to 4000 m altitude (the datasheet notes derating at 2000 m). Noise emission is up to 70 dB: the cabinet is not meant for noise-sensitive areas such as housing, offices and schools, and where it has to stand in one, it is placed at least 40 m away from it. For sites within 5 km of the sea, the warranty terms set limits that depend on the corrosion class of the enclosure (C4 as standard, C5 optional); such sites are agreed before the order. Installation has to be completed within six months of the manufacturing date.
qas.product: GoodWe ESA GW125/261-ESA-LCN-G10 (125 kW / 261 kWh all-in-one storage cabinet)

qas.q: What warranty applies to the cabinet?
qas.a: The GoodWe limited warranty for Europe applies: 5 years on the electronics hardware and the enclosure; 2 years on the liquid-cooling unit, the fire suppression system and the lock cylinder, or 5 years when the system is connected to SEMS+. The performance warranty covers the battery cells for 10 years: 70% of the usable energy of 261.25 kWh or 6000 full charge cycles, whichever comes first. The warranty starts with the first installation or six months after the production date, whichever is earlier. The terms cover up to two full cycles per day and operation with GoodWe inverters; inverters of other brands are checked for compatibility beforehand. The full terms are in the warranty document on this page.
qas.product: GoodWe ESA GW125/261-ESA-LCN-G10 (125 kW / 261 kWh all-in-one storage cabinet)

qas.q: How many inverters does one eManager manage in a parallel system?
qas.a: Up to six. Over RS485 the eManager has three port pairs (A1/B1, A2/B2 and A3/B3); each pair takes at most two inverters, and they must be of the same type. The HS2-(5K-10K)-T2 systems connect over RS485; the H2-(10K-30K)-(T2, T3) hybrid inverters connect over the LAN port and a network switch.

qas.q: Which inverter firmware does the eManager need?
qas.a: The inverter firmware must not be earlier than: H2-(10K-30K)-(T2, T3): DSP V3.061 and ARM V8.035; HS2-(5K-10K)-T2: DSP V4.066 and ARM V1.070; HS3-(5K-12K)-T2: DSP V2.103 and ARM V2.030. An earlier version is upgraded remotely on the elekeeper web platform or locally over Bluetooth with the elekeeper app.

qas.q: When does the eManager need external current transformers?
qas.a: The built-in current transformers are for a nominal current of 63 A per line conductor. Above 63 A, external current transformers of the type 50×N A / 50 mA with N of 2 or more are connected to the CT ports.

qas.q: For how many CHS2 systems is the eManager-C1 Pro meant?

qas.q: How is the eManager-C1 Pro supplied and mounted?
qas.a: The box takes 9 to 36 V DC or 176 to 300 V AC at 50/60 Hz, with a maximum power of 50 W. It is wall-mounted and has ingress protection IP65.

qas.q: Which SAJ inverters take the eSolar AIO3?
qas.a: The H2-(10K-30K)-(T2, T3) hybrid inverters take it on the 4G/WIFI port and have one in their package. The HS2-(5K-10K)-T2 systems support it as a communication module. The HS3 models with W in the designation have an AIO3 module built in. One module connects one inverter.

qas.q: What do the LEDs on the module show?
qas.a: Green stands for Ethernet, blue for Wi-Fi. Green, slow blink: Ethernet is working; green, fast blink: firmware is upgrading; green, solid: the module is not connected to the server; off: no power supply or program fault. Blue, slow blink: Wi-Fi is working; blue, fast blink: Bluetooth is connected. Slow blink is 1 s on and 1 s off, fast blink 200 ms on and 200 ms off.

qas.q: How is the module installed and connected to the network?
qas.a: The hexagon nut of the module is turned to the horizontal position, the module is inserted into the USB interface of the inverter and the nut is fastened clockwise. For Ethernet, the RJ45 connector is connected to the router. After the inverter is powered on, a slowly blinking signal light after 2 minutes shows that the module is working normally. In the app, the module is selected over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi or Ethernet is chosen for internet access.

qas.q: What does the backup output of the HS2-10K-T2-X deliver when the grid fails?
